title: Scheduler handoff → kernel correlation: time-aligned replay anchors for per-request playback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: improve runtime profiling fidelity by introducing time-aligned anchors that correlate the prefill->decode scheduler handoff with per-GPU kernel execution. Current span stitching relies on NVTX ranges plus best-effort timestamp alignment and frequently misattributes short handoff windows to adjacent kernels. This ticket will design and implement an anchor-based correlation mechanism using lightweight CUDA events + synthetic 'handoff ticks' emitted by the scheduler, with a playback tool that replays per-request traces into a deterministic timeline for debugging and root-cause analysis.
tasks: Design anchor protobuf payload and NVTX naming conventions (use human-readable anchor IDs and hashed exec IDs)
Add scheduler emit points: prefill-complete, prefill-to-decode-handoff, decode-start (emit CUDA event and NVTX range)
Instrument kernel submit path to attach nearest anchor IDs and wall-clock offsets to kernel metrics
Update tracing pipeline: accept anchorIDs and map CUDA events to spans in the collector
Build a lightweight replay CLI that consumes per-request artifacts (anchors, kernel metrics, nvtx traces) and produces a time-aligned waterfall visualization
Add unit + integration tests for anchor propagation across worker threads and RPC boundaries
Create dashboards: anchor failure rate, average handoff latency, anchor-to-kernel attribution accuracy
acceptance_criteria: Anchor emitted on scheduler handoff for >=99% of requests in our perf CI workload
Mean anchor-to-first-kernel latency measured and visible in dashboard; regressions flagged by alert
Replay tool can replay a 10k-token request and align 95% of kernel call entries within a 2ms window of wall-clock timeline
PRs merged that add anchor fields to kernel metrics and collector parsing with backward-compatible schema handling
Documentation and runbook added describing how to use anchors to diagnose decode stalls

notes: Trade-offs considered: NVTX-only approach is simplest but brittle under stream multiplexing; CUDA events add small runtime cost but provide authoritative ordering. For Dedicated customers we gate anchor emission behind a flag to avoid changing kernel submission paths unless enabled. Future: consider hardware timestamps if available to replace synthetic anchors.
